To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
our proposed method can be used to recognize human action in videos of arbitrary length and size using multiple features.
we propose a novel 3-D-ConvNet architecture, called Two-stream 3-DCNN Fusion, for action recognition in video with arbitrary size and length.

1) we propose a novel end-to-end framework for action recognition in video of arbitrary size and arbitrary length, 2) we propose two novel models, STPP and LSTM/CNN-E, to extract global description from the input video, 3) we propose a late fusion to fuse the features from the two streams, 4) our method outperformed the state-of-the art on three standard benchmark action recognition datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two important issues in video action recognition: 1) how to extract features for variable-size videos and 2) how to combine features from different streams for better recognition performance.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method can recognize human actions from videos of arbitrary size, length, and content.
our method can achieve state-of-the-art results for action recognition in arbitrary-sized and arbitrary-length video shots.

our method is the first 3-D-ConvNet-based method that can recognize human actions from videos of arbitrary size, and our method is the best-performed method on the three standard action recognition benchmark datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our method can be applied to videos of arbitrary size (e.g., $112 \times 112$, $224 \times 224$, $256 \times 256$ or $480 \times 640$), and arbitrary length (e.g., from 16 to 200 frames) with a high recognition rate.
our proposed method can achieve state-of-the-art results for action recognition in arbitrary-sized and arbitrary-length videos.

we present a novel end-to-end video analysis pipeline, which can be easily applied to videos with arbitrary size and length, and it achieves the state-of-the-arts on the three standard benchmark datasets for human action recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method is a general framework for 3-D convNets to handle videos of arbitrary size, and we believe that our method will be a useful tool for video analysis.
3-D convNets can be extended to videos of arbitrary sizes and lengths, and our method can be easily extended to other 3-D CNN based methods.
the proposed method can recognize human actions from a video of arbitrary size and/or length, which has never been achieved before.
